detail: Said during Student 3's question about a fifth request when servers 1 and 3 both have the least connections; the words sit inside the student's turn, apparently the teacher interjecting. The teacher then answered that the student assumes a server handles only one query (see K1-087).
speaker: teacher

statement: Uniform infrastructure, where every machine behind the load balancer has the same configuration, is true in most cases.
detail: Said while explaining why round robin distributes load almost equally; the referent of 'in most cases it is true' is not fully clear.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: because you have uniform infrastructure, each machine having the same configuration, in most cases it is true

statement: The orchestrator's health checks on backend servers follow the same idea as the earlier online/offline indicator design; how exactly you implement them is up to you.
detail: Said right before 'Typically orchestrator itself makes those HTTP calls to each of the servers and needs to get a 200 response.' The link to the online/offline indicator is made explicit again in the closing Q&A (K3-071, K3-099).
speaker: teacher
verbatim: Now again, pick online off-line indicator. However, you may want to implement it either.
flags: check: 'pick online off-line indicator' as heard - probably 'think of the online/offline indicator'

statement: The goal is to understand the intuition behind a design, not to mug things up; the teacher will stretch the session rather than compromise on quality to get there.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: I want all of you to understand the intuition rather than just mugging things up

statement: How the lock store was chosen: first define what must be stored (resource and owner), then the edge case (a holder dying without releasing), then the key features required from the database (key-value access, atomic instructions, TTL); only then pick a database that offers them - Redis.
detail: Recap the teacher gave after deriving the Redis-based remote lock: 'We know the key features that we need from the database... We know Redis gives us. So that's why we implement remote lock using Redis.'
speaker: teacher
verbatim: We defined that what all, how we would store it. What is the edge case and the key features that we need from the database.

statement: A student suggested that the single-connection network lock could avoid the cost of a hosted Redis; the teacher replied that you still need the other parts.
detail: The student's turn is partly unclear; the teacher's reply is only "Other parts. You need those things.", so what the other parts are is not stated. No clear verdict on the cost argument.
speaker: student (proposal)
verbatim: So couldn't we prevent the cost? I mean, if Redis is hosted service, we prevent the cause.
